attacks.claim: The first-pass quadratic-backtracking claim is technically valid but low impact. TRAILING_PUNCT can go quadratic on a URL token with a very long punctuation run followed by a non-punctuation character. It needs tens of thousands of characters and a hostile neighbor. A server-side length cap on description would close it.
attacks.evidence: const TRAILING_PUNCT = /[.,;:!?)\]]+$/; ABSENT: any max description length

attacks.claim: A leading link is shown whole even when it exceeds the limit, and no wrapping rule is added. A very long unbroken URL can overflow on phones. Plain text overflowed the same way before this PR, so it is not a regression.
attacks.evidence: out.push(t); // a leading link is shown whole rather than collapsing to nothing

attacks.claim: The PR says truncation only cuts at whitespace or between tokens. The fallback cuts mid-word for a leading whitespace-free text token, and the tests assert this behavior.

A description whose overflow past the limit is only trailing whitespace still gets truncated=true. This shows a 'Show more' toggle that reveals nothing new. Trailing ')' is also stripped from URLs unconditionally, which breaks balanced-parenthesis URLs.
attacks.evidence: return { tokens: out, truncated: true }; const TRAILING_PUNCT = /[.,;:!?)\]]+$/;

attacks.claim: Links open in a new tab (target=_blank) with no indication for screen-reader users.
attacks.evidence: <a key={i} href={t.href} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">
